answer: Forced pairing plus decay keeps a sybil farm expensive. Each epoch a newcomer is paired with two established members; each audits and signs the other's work. Standing is not a stored balance: it halves every few epochs and survives only if the holder returns and is re-vouched by a new partner. A thousand keys must rent a thousand distinct partners, fund a thousand submissions and repeat it each epoch, since the orchard of trust rots, not ripens. The atlas of vouchers is public, so a self-vouching ring is a closed loop that one falcon strike ends. Identities cannot be stockpiled, only fed.
